podcast.title: Resignation from Elvis's Band (September 1957)
podcast.body: Bill Black, alongside Scotty Moore, resigned from Elvis's band in September 1957 due to financial hardship and Colonel Parker's restrictive control. They were salaried, faced a dramatically reduced concert schedule (only 14 shows all year), and felt unable to communicate with Elvis, leading to accumulating debt. "In September, Scotty Moore and Bill Black had written to Elvis, resigning from his band."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Conditions for Rejoining Elvis and Permanent Departure (1958)
podcast.body: After his initial resignation and Elvis's attempt to replace him, Bill Black was offered his job back, with a per diem arrangement. However, after the very next recording sessions, Bill Black never again recorded with Elvis, being replaced by Bob Moore in the studio. Unlike Scotty Moore, Bill Black never worked with Elvis again after Elvis joined the army, choosing to focus on his own career. "But after the next recording sessions, Bill never again recorded with Elvis."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Formation of Bill Black's Combo (Post-1958)
podcast.body: After Elvis entered the army, Bill Black formed his own instrumental group, Bill Black's Combo. This band went on to have several instrumental hits over the subsequent years. "Bill Black, meanwhile, formed Bill Black's combo, who had a number of instrumental hits over the next few years."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Illness and Death (1965)
podcast.body: By the time Bill Black's Combo opened for The Beatles' first US tour, Bill Black himself was too ill to join them, and the group toured without him. He tragically died in 1965 at the young age of 39 from a brain tumor. "Unfortunately, by that point, Black himself was too ill to tour, and he had to send the group out without him."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Be-Bop-A-Lula Anecdote
podcast.body: An anecdote from the era claimed that Bill Black, alongside Scotty Moore, was upset with Elvis Presley for supposedly recording "Be-Bop-A-Lula" without their involvement. This story, however, is largely dismissed as improbable. "There are various stories that went round at the time, including that Scotty and Bill got annoyed as Elvis for recording it without them..."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.body: Bill Black was part of the gang of teenage boys that Johnny and Dorsey Burnette used to hang around with and sing alongside in Lauderdale Court. "sing with the gang of teenage boys that included Bill Blacks for the Johnny."

podcast.title: Excluded from Film Soundtrack
podcast.body: Bill Black was not allowed to play on the soundtrack for Elvis Presley's first film, "Doreen O'Brothers" (later "Love Me Tender"), as the film company replaced Elvis's regular band with Hollywood session musicians. "he wasn't allowed to use Scotty Bill and DJ on the soundtrack, because the film company didn't think they could sound hillbilly enough."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Initial Dislike of the Precision Bass
podcast.body: Bill Black, the bass player for Elvis Presley, initially harbored a strong dislike for the Fender Precision Bass. He reportedly struggled to master the instrument and found it difficult to play. "Then came Bill Black, the bass player for Elvis Presley, although it is said that he initially really, really hated the thing because he just couldn't quite get the knack of playing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Story of the Electric Guitar - Part 1

podcast.title: Success of Bill Black's Combo (1960s)
podcast.body: Bill Black's Combo achieved significant popularity, scoring eight Top 40 hits. Their success led them to be chosen as the opening act for The Beatles' first US tour. "Bill Black's combo had eight top 40 hits, and were popular enough that they became the opening act for the Beatles' first US tour."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

concerts.title: The Beatles' first US tour (Bill Black's Combo opened, but Black was too ill to join)

xref.title: Opening Act for The Beatles (1964)
xref.body: Bill Black's Combo served as an opening act for The Beatles' concert at Maple Leaf Gardens in Toronto on September 6, 1964. However, like the other supporting acts, they were met with boos from the impatient crowd, who were exclusively eager to see The Beatles perform. "As the opening bands, which included Bill Black's combo...hit the stage to crowd-bood, they only wanted one band, and one band only."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Opening Acts Booed by Impatient Crowd (1964)
xref.body: At the Maple Leaf Gardens concert in Toronto on September 6, 1964, the opening bands, which included Bill Black's Combo, The Exciters, Clarence "Frogman" Henry, and Jackie De Shannon, were met with boos from the crowd. The audience was impatient and made it clear they wanted only one band: The Beatles. "As the opening bands, which included Bill Black's combo, the exciders Clarence Frogman Henry, and the Celterie Jackie De Shannon hit the stage to crowd-bood, they only wanted one band, and one band only."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
